about: Bar and behaviour lines shaped like those of 17 real runs (reworded; u1213's line is quoted from the public old-run-0.5 fixture). On the real 158 lines the narrow check flags 2: u1213 and one 'every claim true of …'. 'fine' lines must not be flagged, 'open' lines must be.
fine: The dashboard count, the profiles count and the filtered list agree for every standing on the same data
Given any filter set on the list endpoint, when the response is read, then it carries counts computed with every filter except the count's own
Given an admin of another company asks for a person's history, then they get 403 or 404; admins in scope get all of it.
It should add every new template in en, ar and ur marked awaiting approval, and change no approved template.
It should link the platform dashboard to an all-employers list, and each employer profile shows only its own rows.
It should show no raw status value, have every string in en, ar and ur, and work at 360px and right to left (screenshots).
Every date list ordered, id tiebreak on paged lists, queues oldest first, no in-memory caps
Given every date list query in the issue, when read, then each has ORDER BY ending in id
Every event time says its zone; detail shows seconds and UTC; same instant reads the same in any browser zone
Every behaviour below passes on the PR head, judged by a full review plus security and visual critics
Given the new strings, then en, ar and ur all have them (locale parity tests pass), and the panel reads correctly in Arabic RTL and dark mode
doctor checks every setup item with a fix line each; init asks what the person needs and writes it; tests
Catch-up job reruns the three missed exports
every key in the committed en.json has an ar entry
every route listed in routes.md returns 403 without the permission
It shows totals in SAR with two decimals, in English and Arabic
No message is sent twice for the same event
Given an HR admin without the permission, when they open /hr/payroll, then they get a 403 and no data.
open: #1213: every 'we notified / our team has been told' message comes from the same call that sends the notice; a test fails when a claim has no matching notice; the four money-path cases and HR bell for new requests covered
Any "your employer was told" message is backed by a real notice
Catch every leaked secret in the logs
It should never log a token anywhere
every message that claims we told someone is true
It accepts any phrasing of the consent question
